items.headline: Eddie AI Overhauled - Pay-As-You-Go Pricing, Editing from Claude and ChatGPT, and an iPhone App
items.excerpt: Eddie AI drops subscriptions for a credit model and exposes roughly 100 tools over MCP, so editors can drive a rough cut from inside Claude or ChatGPT. Exports still land in Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve and Final Cut, and a new iPhone app handles prompts and review on the move.

items.headline: Digital (De-)Aging and the Uncanny Valley Problem
items.excerpt: A craft breakdown of how aging and de-aging actually get built now, from prosthetics through Benjamin Button and Rogue One to today's ML-driven face pipelines. It maps why even expensive AI-assisted work still falls into the uncanny valley, and what supervisors do about it.

items.headline: You Can Now Run Eddie AI as an MCP Server, Unlocking Pay-As-You-Go Use for AI Assistant Editing
items.excerpt: No Film School walks through Eddie AI's shift to pay-as-you-go credits and its new MCP server, which lets assistant-editor tasks run from Claude or ChatGPT. The angle is what this does to the cost floor of long-form assembly for small teams.

items.headline: USC Adds Beeble AI Production Tools to Filmmaking Courses
items.excerpt: The ETC think tank inside USC's School of Cinematic Arts has folded Beeble's relighting, compositing and scene-reconstruction tech into coursework and research. Students now use the AI toolset hands-on across VFX, virtual production and visual storytelling.

items.headline: HaZ Dulull's 'Astro Burn' Game Comes to Life as AI-Assisted Micro-Series
items.excerpt: A self-described genAI skeptic turned his retro game into ten daily vertical shorts with Nura Studios on the Showcraft platform, using a locked-down model trained only on his own assets. It is a concrete template for IP-safe AI production and vertical distribution.

items.headline: Adobe Unveils New Photoshop AI Tools
items.excerpt: Adobe rolls out a new wave of generative tools in Photoshop, aimed at concept, matte and key-art work that feeds film and animation pipelines. AWN frames the release around what changes for artists working on production art.

items.headline: The power of on-premises open-weight models for generative media
items.excerpt: fxguide argues the practical case for running open-weight generative models on-prem in VFX facilities: workflow stability, client data security, predictable cost and delivery reliability. It is a direct answer to studios that cannot send plates to a cloud API.

items.headline: New CG software you may have missed: 23 August 2026 (Slapshot Comfy nodes, Topaz Hyperion 2.5)
items.excerpt: Slapshot's AI rotoscoping, camera tracking, motion-vector and depth tools are now Comfy nodes at $0.25 per processed frame, pulling core VFX prep into generative pipelines. The same roundup covers Topaz Hyperion 2.5 SDR-to-HDR conversion and Postshot 1.1.69 for Gaussian splats.

items.headline: Filmmaking research and production courses at ETC use Beeble
items.excerpt: ProVideo Coalition covers USC's Entertainment Technology Center adopting Beeble's AI relighting and scene-reconstruction stack for its filmmaking research and production courses. It signals AI compositing moving into how the next crew generation is trained.

items.headline: Six thousand people made a three-minute film about a future worth living in
items.excerpt: Six thousand filmmakers submitted three-minute optimistic-future shorts to the Future Vision XPRIZE with no restriction on toolset, so generative pipelines sat alongside traditional ones. Ten finalists screen live in LA on September 25 with a $2.5M grant on the line.
